chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Stan Kenton asks for Earl Hines-style charts
summary: Pianist Stan Kenton befriends Budd in Arnheim's band and asks for arrangements in Earl Hines's manner.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So, I joined Gus Arnheim's band as the arranger right there. Well, I noticed the piano player. He liked me and he kept, you know -- he says, "Come on up to the room and have dinner with me." And, he would have room service and we would eat steaks and what not. And, so, you know who
Stan Kenton was the piano player in the band. And, he said, "Gee, I sure like -- I sure like the way you write right." He says, "Can you write some of them Earl things for me? The Earl Hines things."

I said, "Well, man, I don't if anybody can really write like Earl plays please." I say, "But, I'll try to write some of the changes and things for you and what not like that, you know." So, we became very good friends from then on.
